If you're wavering on whether to install macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple's hefty security fix list might be enough to convince you. And if you plan to stick with an older version, you may want to install macOS Tahoe 26.7 or macOS Sequoia 15.8 as soon as possible. Here's why.

Apple Patches Over 200 macOS Vulnerabilities

Apple today released full security update notes for macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7, and macOS Sequoia 15.8, detailing more than 200 vulnerabilities patched in this update.

As with recent macOS updates, Apple's acknowledgements include several AI-focused security teams and researchers, including OpenAI Codex Security, NVIDIA AI Red Team, and Anthropic Research.

The patches in macOS 27 cover many categories of vulnerabilities, including ones that could allow malicious apps or attackers to execute arbitrary code with kernel or root privileges, escape the macOS sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper protections, modify protected system files, access sensitive user data, and more.

For example, an AVEVideoEncoder vulnerability could allow a sandboxed app to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges. Meanwhile, a UDF file system vulnerability could also let an app execute code at the kernel level. Apple also patched flaws that could lead to remote code execution via Bluetooth, CUPS, and WebDAV.

For macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8, both updates address many of the same vulnerabilities, including some of the above kernel-level, root privilege, sandbox escape, Gatekeeper bypass, and remote code execution flaws.

The older system versions also have some additional patches not listed in macOS 27, including an ImageIO vulnerability in macOS Sequoia 15.8 that could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing a specially crafted malicious image.
